sourceInformation.source: Chopper Command (1982), Activision; designed by Bob Whitehead
sourceInformation.genre: Arcade shooter / convoy defense / flight action
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with WebGL 2 fallback; Rapier 2D 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio; esbuild 0.28.2
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel shading with three lighting bands, ink outlines, layered desert mesas, teal and vermilion aircraft, cream field-manual UI; embedded Barlow Condensed Black by Jeremy Tribby (SIL Open Font License).
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and NumberKeyframeTrack for main rotors, tail rotors, truck wheels and pickups; procedural banking, camera tracking and particles
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated synth music at 10% default volume, rotor modulation, laser and explosion effects, synthesized Animalese-style radio gibberish; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, client 1.4.0: synchronized parallel score competition for 1–4 players. Standalone supports 1–2 local co-op pilots.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless simulation and browser automation, scripted full campaign, emulated standard-mapping gamepads, touch emulation, Web Audio analyser checks, AI Hub automatic harness, screenshots for appearance
sourceInformation.research: Activision 1982 manual via AtariAge/AtariOnline: convoy defense, scanner, 12 aircraft, splitting missiles, unlimited fire, reserves and scoring. Contemporary Video Swapper and Electronic Fun coverage: desert palette, rotor and laser sound, rotating wheels. Official Three.js, Rapier and AI Hub documentation.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu on WSL2

testingFeedback: 10 issues found and fixed across automated tests, visual checks and integration review: reserve bonuses, pause audio, post-round audio, dead-pilot targeting, co-op framing, first-touch launch, title font, mirrored aircraft details, controller focus and short-screen layout. All 78 automated cases pass.
1 critical input issue: the first touch could move the launch button before the click landed. Touch layout now initializes before interaction.

The scripted full three-sortie campaign at default weapon settings: real Rapier laser collisions exercise enemy waves, splitting missiles, shield, pickups, the airship and victory. The official Hub harness also verified multiplayer lifecycle.
Headless WebGPU screenshots were blank despite verified rendering frames. WebGL fallback screenshots were useful for visual inspection instead.
engineFeedback: Three.js node materials make crisp cel bands straightforward, and AnimationMixer fits mechanical animation well.
Headless WebGPU rendered frames but produced blank canvas captures; appearance was inspected with the renderer's WebGL 2 fallback.
The convoy-defense simulation, wave director, controller navigation, synthesized audio and complete gameplay UI.
Combining WebGPU material support, native animation, wrapped world coordinates and reliable browser verification in one portable file.
More reliable headless WebGPU canvas capture and clearer diagnostics for the active rendering backend.
promptFeedback: The specific source research, attract-mode requirement and controller-first direction gave the demo a clear identity.
The online link initially leaves the choice between parallel competition and a shared world open; the protocol resolves the implementation details.
Delivering every gameplay system, multiple input methods, audio and multiplayer protocol in a single tested HTML file.
State the preferred multiplayer mode and whether a WebGL fallback is welcome when WebGPU is unavailable.

aiHub.name: Chop Shop Command
aiHub.tagline: Low flight. High stakes. Special delivery.
aiHub.description: Fly cover for twelve medicine trucks through a cel-shaded desert. Dodge splitting missiles, shield the convoy, and bring down a command airship across three escalating sorties.
aiHub.controls: Left stick/WASD fly; right stick/mouse aim; R2/Cross/Space fire; Square/E convoy shield; R1/Shift boost; Options/Esc pause. Local P2: IJKL/N/M/U or second pad.
